self.fit_target = None
        screen = self.get_screen()
        resize_handler = screen.connect("size-changed", lambda *_: self.size_for_field_screen(self, self.get_allocation()))
        self.connect("destroy", lambda *_: screen.disconnect(resize_handler))
        width, height = area.width, area.height
        target = None
        if self.get_window():
            monitor = self.get_display().get_monitor_at_window(self.get_window())
            if monitor:
                bounds = monitor.get_workarea()
                if bounds.width > 0 and bounds.height > 0 and (width > bounds.width or height > bounds.height):
                    # GTK may retain the previous monitor's minimum width on rotation.
                    width, height = bounds.width, bounds.height
                    target = (width, height)
        if target != self.fit_target:
            self.fit_target = target
            if target:
                # GTK recalculates styled requisitions over subsequent display frames.
                GLib.timeout_add(40, self.finish_monitor_resize, target, time.monotonic()+0.7)
        # A tall screen still has to fit three side-by-side decision buttons.
        factor = width / 480
        if width >= height:
            factor = max(factor, height / 296)
        scale = max(1, round(factor, 1))

    def finish_monitor_resize(self, target, deadline):
        if target != self.fit_target or not self.get_realized() or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            return False
        self.resize(*target)
        return True
